thread:
alex: Heads up — several prod deploys started failing around 01:23 UTC with 403 from deploy-bot when it tries to impersonate ci-service-sa. Auto-rollback triggered.
maya: @alex can you paste the exact error snippet and which pipeline ran?
alex: pipeline: release/main->prod. Error log: 
```
2026-03-15T01:23:10Z deploy-bot[pid:4123]: impersonate ci-service-sa -> 403 PermissionDenied
{"error":"PermissionDenied","status":403,"detail":"serviceAccounts.getAccessToken: caller does not have permission to generate token for ci-service-sa"}
```
sam: we're seeing same in staging runner — job failed mid-step. Noticed runner token TTL set to 60s in .gitlab-ci.yml, so token might expire while step runs.
support-oncall: @maya @sam please check if recent SA rotation went out at ~01:22:58. Could be a rotation race where the token was revoked server-side while runner still used it.
maya: Confirmed — ops rotated keys at 01:22:58 (new rotation daemon release). Rotation revokes previous ephemeral tokens as part of hardening. That lines up with failures.
jordan: Quick repro I did (local):
1) start pipeline that calls /v1/deploys
2) trigger rotation script to revoke old tokens
3) curl using cached token returns 403 mid-flight
```
TOKEN="<old-token>"
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/deploys
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"service account token invalidated"}
```
alex: Temporary mitigation: paused rotation job and restarted a subset of runners — deploy succeeded after restarts. But this is not acceptable long term.
liam: Root cause theory: rotation revokes token reference before CI obtains fresh credentials. Two options: 1) make rotation staggered with drain window, 2) change CI to use IAM impersonation flow (iamcredentials.generateAccessToken) so token issuance is atomic and not invalidated by key revocation. Also add retry/backoff for 403.
support-oncall: Also verify that ci-service-sa currently has overly broad roles (it had roles/editor from earlier onboarding). Least-privilege checklist: only grant iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken (or iam.serviceAccounts.actAs if using impersonation), and the specific runtime/data roles required.
sam: I'll open an urgent change: increase runner token TTL to 5m, add retry logic around deploy call (3 retries with exponential backoff), and schedule a staggered rotation window at 02:00 UTC with runner restarts.
maya: Ops will change rotation daemon to perform a rolling revoke (revokes old tokens only after new tokens are confirmed issued to all active runner pools). We'll also instrument a metric for "token-refresh-failures".
alex: Marking as P0 since prod deploys blocked. :bangbang:
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-43 — severity: P0, assignees: sam, maya. Created by alex.
maya: Noted, coordinating now. I'll post a 30m update. :thumbsup:
sam: Opening PR with TTL + retry patches and a short runbook for restoring paused rotation: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge_requests/788 (WIP)
alex: Thanks — please @me when PR is merged and when rotation is resumed.
liam: Long-term action items: switch CI auth to short-lived impersonation tokens (workload identity where applicable), implement graceful rotation with drain window, tighten SA RBAC, and add canary deploy step that verifies token behavior before full rollout.
support-oncall: Adding those to INC ticket. If anyone spots new 403s post-fix, ping this thread and attach runner logs. :eyes:
